text:
maria: Heads-up — after today's runtime deploy we're seeing TP+PP jobs lose comm/compute overlap, throughput down ~30%. nvtx traces show long idle gaps during all-reduce windows.

sam: Thanks, any links to traces? :eyes:

maria: https://ci.internal/redwood/traces/4821 (nvtx timeline + exported flame)

perf-bot: Profiling job 4821 finished. Summary: allreduce idle time 48% (baseline 17%), kernel time down 10%, end-to-end latency +28%.

jing: Quick note: I think this is related to the cudaGraph replay changes in the kvcache path. Found a suspicious pattern in the runtime: the graph for KV prefetch is being launched on the main compute stream instead of the dedicated kvcache_stream.

sam: That would easily serialize things. Which PR introduced that? I remember a fallback path for kernel selection changed launch semantics.

maria: PR #2123 touched graph-launch logic and the kernel fallback shim. Logs show: "fused_attention_v2 -> fallback: launch_simple_attn" followed by "kv_prefetch: graph_launch main_stream".

jing: Concrete snippet from runtime (simplified):
```
// kvcache prefetch
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, kvcache_stream);
cudaGraphInstantiate(&g, ...); // capture happened on kvcache_stream
// bug: launching on main stream
cudaGraphLaunch(g, main_stream);
``` 
That cross-stream launch creates an implicit dependency when the capture had events on kvcache_stream.

sam: Right — launching a graph on main_stream when it contains ops from kvcache_stream can cause implicit stream synchronization if events/waits are used. Also cudaGraph replay captures ordering which can pin host-side sync points.

maria: NVTX shows we have an event recorded on kvcache_stream that main_stream later waits on (cudaStreamWaitEvent). The wait came from the graph-launch translation we added.

perf-bot: Detailed flame excerpt: 
"allreduce(start) -> wait_for_event(14.3ms) -> compute_resume(2.1ms)" repeated across steps. NCCL queue shows backpressure while main_stream holds serialized ops.

sam: Another angle: kernel selection fallback now picks a non-vectorized kernel that issues an extra host->device memcpy for small batches. That memcpy is enqueued to the main_stream in fallback path, so small-batch fallback increases host stalls in main_stream.

jing: So two compounding issues: 1) graph launch on wrong stream causing stream-ordering wait, 2) fallback kernel enqueues extra memcpy on main_stream causing host syncs. Together they kill overlap and increase allreduce stalls.

maria: Repro steps I used:
```
export RW_RUNTIME=canary
python -m experiments.tp_pp --model gpt-xl --seq 1024 --batch 4 --profile nvtx --nvprof
```
Observes the gap within 3 steps.

sam: Do we have a quick mitigation? Rollback runtime change or force graph launches to use dedicated kvcache_stream and isolate fallback memcpys to low-prio streams.

jing: I'll whip up a hotfix to ensure graph launches use the original capture stream: if (graph_capture_stream != launch_stream) then cudaGraphInstantiate+Launch on capture_stream, or at least enqueue a non-blocking stream-copy rather than streamWaitEvent.

maria: Also add a unit test in the replay harness that asserts comm/compute overlap >= X% for a synthetic TP+PP scenario to catch regressions.

perf-bot: Creating regression alert: perf-regression-4821, threshold breach: comm-overlap < 60%.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling back runtime v1.9.3 -> v1.9.2 initiated (canary pool). :warning:

sam: Thanks. Jing — want me to pair on the hotfix PR? I can point to the failing trace and the PR that introduced the change.

jing: Yes please. I'll open PR with revert + targeted fix and include the repro script & nvtx assert. ETA 2 hours.

maria: Great. After hotfix lands let's run the full tensor/pipeline parallel perf suite on 4xA100 to confirm allreduce latency returns to baseline.

sam: I'll schedule that run and post results here.

maria: :thumbsup:
